name: awesome-agent-skills-security
description: 🛡️ A curated list of resources on agent skills security: attacks, defenses, frameworks, and benchmarks for securing AI agent tool use and skill ecosystems

paragraphs: 🛡️ A curated list of resources on securing AI agent tool use and skill ecosystems — attacks, defenses, frameworks, benchmarks, and standards.

AI agents increasingly use external tools, plugins, and skills to interact with the world. This creates a new attack surface: agent skills security. This list covers the threats, defenses, and research landscape for securing these capabilities.

whatItDoes.text: 🛡️ A curated list of resources on securing AI agent tool use and skill ecosystems — attacks, defenses, frameworks, benchmarks, and standards.

requirements.text: Studies proactive over-authorization, where tool-calling agents retrieve more private data than a request requires; introduces the OverAct benchmark (eight privacy-sensitive domains, deterministic judge-free scoring) and finds all seven tested models significantly exceed authorized scope, with request specificity the strongest severity predictor and a cost-asymmetry account…

Black-box, task-agnostic attack that uses fuzzing-generated page-specific indirect injections to make login appear a plausible prerequisite for continuing the task, luring LLM web agents onto attacker-controlled login pages for end-to-end credential and private-data leakage — reaching 86% average success across LLM backbones and remaining effective across agent architectures…
📄 Self-State Attacks on Self-Hosted AI Agents: How Far Can OS Defenses Go? — Chen et al., 2026.

Formalizes a threat class in which a self-hosted agent is compromised by corrupting its own state through legitimate OS system-call invocations, then evaluates layered OS-level defenses to expose the residual vulnerabilities they cannot close.
